## Background

Paper 003 studies firm-level AI measurement by organizing indicators into technology, business-purpose, and acquisition dimensions. The larger design builds on research connecting AI use and firm productivity [@czarnitzki2023]. This coursework subproject demonstrates provenance and reproducible reporting rather than making substantive claims; transparent computational records are central to that goal [@sandve2013].

Related studies distinguish AI technologies, uses, and sourcing strategies in German and French firms [@rammer2022; @calvino2026].

The included dataset is fake and contains no actual research data or firm observations. Its 10 teaching-example rows represent only a small part of the codebook: each row describes a variable associated with an IKT, CIS, REGN, or VoF source file. It must not be interpreted as the complete codebook or an analytical sample.

## Visualization

The included R script, `R/0103030409_generate_mmc_v01_sunburst_weight_graphs.r`, generates the non-faceted 2021 M1 sunburst shown below. The graph illustrates aggregate fitted AI-adoption weights across the Technology, Purpose, and Acquisition hierarchy and contains no firm-level observations. Running the script requires supporting inputs and shared functions from the parent project; the included PDF preserves its output for this self-contained report.

```{=html}
<figure id="fig-production-sunburst">
  <object data="figures/sun_m1_h_y21.pdf" type="application/pdf" width="100%" height="720">
    <p><a href="figures/sun_m1_h_y21.pdf">Open the sunburst PDF.</a></p>
  </object>
  <figcaption>M1 sunburst for the annual-harmonised 2021 fit.</figcaption>
</figure>
```

## Graphical grammar

The visualization uses a consistent graphical grammar to make the model hierarchy legible:

- **Structure:** a sunburst places **AI Adoption** at the center, dimensions in the inner ring, and indicators in the outer ring.
- **Order:** sectors begin at 12 o'clock and proceed clockwise through Technology, Purpose, and Acquisition.
- **Color:** Technology uses blue (`#0072B2`), Purpose orange (`#D55E00`), and Acquisition green (`#009E73`); indicator shades remain within the corresponding dimension hue.
- **Typography and boundaries:** Arial labels, restrained gray guides, and white internal borders separate the hierarchy without adding visual clutter.
- **Output:** the figure is exported as a Cairo PDF, with a corresponding text caption in the parent workflow.

## Reproducibility scope

The Quarto report renders from the included fake metadata, bibliography, citation style, and graph. The R script records how the graph is generated, but regenerating it requires the parent project's shared graph helper, configuration, and aggregate fitted-weight inputs.
